guitar.guitaristsText: Keith Richards / Ronnie Wood / Mick Taylor
guitar.modelsText: Fender Telecaster ('Micawber', 5-string open-G) / Gibson Les Paul / ES series
guitar.evidence: Keith Richards' 5-string open-G-tuned Telecaster 'Micawber' is one of the most famous specific guitars in rock history; this justifies high rather than medium confidence.
guitar.notes: Upgraded confidence from medium to high due to Richards' very specifically documented guitar/tuning setup.

tone.target: raw 60s garage crunch with slight fuzz bite
tone.profile: raw 60s garage crunch with slight fuzz bite
tone.summary: A gritty signal chain using a Tube Screamer boost into an AC30-style amp, followed by a vintage British cabinet to capture the raw, nasal sound of early Stones recordings.
corrections: less warm blues, more ragged bite

rig.name: The Rolling Stones - Get Off Of My Cloud - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Simulate the aggressive, mid-focused bite of a Tube Screamer/overdrive pedal to push the amp into natural grit.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is chosen for its punchy, non-modern overdrive character, fitting the 'garage crunch' requirement better than Blues OD or OD 9.

blocks.purpose: Add the required 'slight fuzz texture' and ragged bite without sounding overly modern or high-gain.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze provides a classic, slightly woolly fuzz that complements the mid-range focus of the Green OD, achieving the desired 'garage fuzz'.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the classic British combo sound (AC30) known for its nasal, mid-heavy character and natural breakup.
Provide the classic British cabinet voicing and raw sound character.
Slightly boost the mids to enhance the 'nasal bite' and cut through the mix, while taming excessive low end.
Disabled. Chorus is explicitly avoided by the musical verdict to maintain a raw, dry 60s feel.
blocks.gap: The module is included but deactivated as per instructions and musical constraints.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle space and dimension without sounding modern or overly processed.
blocks.gap: A very minimal delay is used to add depth, avoiding the 'modern overdrive polish' feel. Settings are kept low.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle sense of space and room ambience without washing out the raw tone.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is used sparingly to give depth, avoiding excessive wash that would ruin the 'raw mono feel'.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to enhance the raw, nasal 60s garage sound.

proposals.recommendedAsset: vintage British combo IR (e.g., early Vox/AC30)
proposals.reason: The current cabinet needs a more authentic, raw 60s voicing to match the Stones' sound.
